Appointment Readiness: Representatives and Key Individuals

Let us start with the role you are preparing for. Representatives and Key Individuals both support compliant financial services, but their responsibilities are not the same.

Let us start with the role you are preparing for. Representatives and Key Individuals both support compliant financial services, but their responsibilities are not the same.

Which role are you preparing for? Select your role, then compare it with the other role.

If you are preparing to be a Representative

You are authorised to render financial services on behalf of TFG Insure, within the scope of its licence and the approved product categories. In practice, this means you must know what you may do, what you may not do, and when to escalate.

Responsibilities

  • Act honestly, fairly and with due care.
  • Treat Customers fairly and support positive outcomes.
  • Give factual, accurate information and remain within the non-advice model.
  • Follow approved scripts, processes and procedures.
  • Complete required training and assessments.
  • Disclose interests and potential conflicts.
  • Keep required records and escalate concerns, complaints, incidents or compliance risks.
Scenario

Imagine a Customer asks you to recommend the “best” option for their personal circumstances. What should you do? Your answer should reflect the non-advice model and the approved escalation process.

If you are preparing to be a Key Individual

You are accountable for managing and overseeing the financial services activities under your responsibility. Your role is to make sure the right people, controls and support are in place.

Responsibilities

  • Oversee financial services activities.
  • Supervise, train and support Representatives.
  • Promote ethical conduct and compliance.
  • Monitor adherence to FAIS and regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure only authorised and competent people render financial services.
  • Escalate material compliance and governance concerns.
  • Support Treating Customers Fairly outcomes.
  • Ensure effective risk controls are in place.
Key takeaway

Readiness means that you can explain your responsibilities and demonstrate the right action when a risk or Customer need arises.

You have explored the responsibilities of Representatives and Key Individuals and considered how each role supports compliant financial services and fair Customer outcomes. Knowing your responsibilities is an important first step. You must also be able to recognise situations that could affect, or appear to affect, your ability to act fairly and objectively.

Next, you will learn how to identify and disclose interests that may create an actual, potential, or perceived conflict of interest.
